user_statement: So both that last display cover and this latest one broke as I was try to place them on the faucet. I confirmed with the previous white pet-gf faucet we printed (which was an older sculpted design, hopefully there is a specific record of it) and it does not snap this easily - even just getting the display into the display cover which is hardly any bend at all, certainly less bend than it takes to get on the faucet, is all it took to break these new display covers.

identified_recent_jobs.scope: Display cover from the complete five-part set; other parts not assessed by this report.

observations.fracture_location: Curved perimeter wall beneath the bezel, with a long detached rim section on one side.
photo_visible_features: Long thin strip separated from the curved wall/rim transition
Several thinner strips and individual extrusion strands bridge the separation
observations.fracture_direction_interpretation: The peeling separation appears broadly parallel to the print-layer courses. This is a photograph-based interpretation, not a measured fracture-plane normal.

scope: The two identified current-cover jobs are rejected for assembly. September accepted-cover evidence is retained for its identified geometry; the report does not reject the other parts in the complete white faucet set.

photo_evidence.identity_scope: One photographed failed cover from the reported recent covers; the photo does not identify which of the two job IDs.

print_orientation.meaning: Layer planes are parallel to the display bezel; the skirt and bezel build successively along local N.

photo_evidence.interpretation: The strips, strands and apparent layer-parallel peeling strengthen weak interlayer or inter-road fusion as the leading failure-mode hypothesis. They do not identify excessive cooling as the cause or exclude a stress concentration at the curved transition.
